title: Farmers were losing a third of their harvest to spoilage. She built a machine to stop that.
sources: India CSR / Schwab Foundation - 2026 Social Entrepreneur of the Year India awardees
Eco-Business - Linking smallholders to markets: Earthshot Prize winner S4S Technologies
caption:
Smallholder farmers across India lose huge amounts of produce to spoilage before it ever reaches a market. Nidhi Pant built a machine small enough to fix that on the farm itself.

Pant co-founded S4S Technologies, building low-cost, solar-powered dehydration units that let farmers and rural women process surplus produce into shelf-stable products instead of losing it. The model has turned rural women into micro-entrepreneurs, with reported income increases of up to 15% for the smallholder farmers it works with.

In 2026, Pant won the Social Entrepreneur of the Year India award from the Jubilant Bhartia and Schwab Foundations - S4S Technologies had already won the Earthshot Prize for the same work.

She didn't build a bigger farm. She built the machine that keeps what was already grown from going to waste.
